column1: CSV file (Excel) containing the county-level results for the HTL Future Scenario detailed in Greene et al.

Conversion to Renewable Diesel via Hydrothermal Liquefaction (HTL) – Future Targets: This future scenario assumes an enhanced biomass composition (similar to nutrient-deplete conditions) leading to improved biocrude yields of 49%.

Future advancements in genetic engineering or lipid accumulation strategies are assumed to achieve higher lipid content without compromising productivity. Nutrient recovery efficiencies are increased to 90% for nitrogen and phosphorus
while DAC costs are reduced to $50/ton with an increased CUE of 90%. These improvements align with optimized targets for renewable diesel production.
